articles.title: The British Royal Family in shock: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle leave the US to return to England
articles.standfirst: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are reportedly preparing for an extended UK stay, with their children set to attend school in Britain and King Charles a major factor in the decision
articles.summary: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are reportedly preparing for an extended UK stay, with their children set to attend school in Britain and King Charles a major factor in the decision
articles.body:
P rince Harry and Meghan Markle are preparing for a major change in family life, with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex reportedly planning to spend an extended period in the UK after more than six years based in the United States .

The move represents a striking development for a couple who left Britain and stepped back as senior working royals in 2020 before establishing a new life in California.

However, reports indicate that this is not a permanent relocation, with the Sussexes expected to retain their $14.5 million Montecito home.

According to Page Six, the couple decided earlier this month to leave California for an extended stay in Britain, with their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet , expected to attend school in the UK.

Sources cited by the publication say that strengthening the children's connections with their wider family is one of the central motivations behind the decision.

A royal insider told Page Six: “I know that Charles is a big reason for their return.”

The timing is particularly significant because Harry and his father, King Charles III , have endured a strained relationship for several years.

Their relationship has shown signs of improvement recently, however, including a meeting at Highgrove during the family's July visit to Britain. Charles and Queen Camilla reportedly hosted Harry, Meghan and their two children at the Gloucestershire residence.

The meeting was especially meaningful because Charles had not seen Archie and Lilibet in person since the Platinum Jubilee in 2022.

Harry and Meghan's children are at the heart of the decision

Archie , seven, and Lilibet , five, are expected to begin their education in Britain, giving them an opportunity to spend considerably more time around relatives and develop stronger relationships with members of the extended family.

The move does not mean, however, that they are suddenly being reintegrated into the working royal family.

King Charles is reportedly supportive of the family's return on a personal level while maintaining the distinction between his son as a private citizen and the working members of the monarchy. The Sussexes are not expected to resume official royal duties.

There is also a considerable obstacle when it comes to Harry's relationship with his brother, Prince William .

Despite the thawing relationship between Harry and his father, reports indicate that the longstanding tension between the two brothers remains.

That means Archie and Lilibet are unlikely to suddenly develop a close relationship with their cousins, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis .

Harry does, however, remain close to his cousin Princess Eugenie . She and her husband, Jack Brooksbank , have maintained a relationship with the Sussexes, while the families have also spent time in Portugal.

The return to Britain is therefore likely to be more complicated than a straightforward royal reconciliation. Harry and Meghan have spent years building independent lives away from the monarchy, and their move does not erase the disputes that led to their departure.

Security remains a major concern for Prince Harry

Perhaps the biggest practical question surrounding the family's return involves security.

Harry has spent years challenging the arrangements governing his protection when he visits Britain. His security status changed after he stopped being a working royal, and the issue has been the subject of a prolonged legal dispute.

Earlier this year, security concerns even complicated plans for Meghan and the children to accompany Harry to Britain. Harry had previously said, “I can’t see a world in which I would bring my wife and children back to the UK at this point.”

A security assessment reported by ITV in July said Harry remained the focus of several terrorist plots, underlining why protection has remained such a sensitive issue for the Sussexes.

Harry is still awaiting a review of his security arrangements by RAVEC, the committee responsible for determining protective arrangements for senior public figures and members of the royal family.

That issue could therefore play an important role in determining how frequently the Sussexes remain in Britain and where they spend their time.

For now, the reported move appears less like a dramatic abandonment of their American life and more like an attempt to establish a second base closer to Harry's family.

After years of distance, the decision could give Charles substantially more opportunities to see his grandchildren while allowing Archie and Lilibet to experience more of their father's home country.

Whether it eventually leads to a deeper reconciliation between Harry and the wider royal family remains uncertain.

But the decision to bring the children to Britain for an extended period represents one of the clearest signs yet that the Sussexes are willing to rebuild part of their connection with the UK.

articles.title: Prince Harry's return to the UK could alter Prince William and King Charles' plans completely
articles.standfirst: This could be a true turning point for the British Royal Family.
articles.summary: This could be a true turning point for the British Royal Family.
articles.body:
The rumors very much appear to be true: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will return to the United Kingdom very soon, and not just for a short business trip or vacation.

According to reports, Harry, Meghan and their children will return to the UK at the end of the month for what is being considered an extended period of time. No one is quite sure how long that will be, but it sounds like it could very much be a long-term decision.

Harry and Meghan reportedly want to enroll their children in British schools, as well as have them be close to their grandfather, King Charles III . Now 77 years old , Charles continues to undergo treatment for his battle with an undisclosed form of cancer.

While Harry's intentions are pure, the elephant in the room is that he and Meghan remain non-working royals. Apparently, that won't change even when they return , given that they're the ones who made the initial decision to renounce their duties when they moved to California.

Prince William will have to swallow pride and can't continue to ignore Prince Harry

Despite that, Harry will certainly still be present at several royal events, especially those which will allow him to be close to Charles . That could prove chaotic, as Prince William does not seem to be on speaking terms with Harry yet . William will have to adapt to the new norm whether he wants to or not, according to royal reporter Tom Sykes .

It’s going to represent huge challenges for William. William is gonna have to figure out how he is going to respond to this. What is going to happen if Charles invites Harry to join the royal family for Christmas? What is going to happen if Harry wants to attend the Remembrance Day celebrations? What is going to happen if his father endorses Harry by appearing in public shoulder to shoulder with him? It’s a huge succession of challenges for William.

Per Sykes, it simply won't be "sustainable" for William to ignore Harry completely once he's back for good.

articles.title: Caught Red-Handed? Meghan Markle slammed for her $35 wine scam... it's cheaper online
articles.standfirst: Customers question the price difference as a similar Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc catches attention
articles.summary: Customers question the price difference as a similar Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc catches attention
articles.body:
M eghan Markle ’s latest As Ever product has found itself at the center of a new debate after shoppers compared the price of her wine with similar bottles available for significantly less.

The Duchess of Sussex ’s lifestyle brand is selling a 2024 Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc for $35 per bottle, but some customers have pointed out that comparable New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc options can be purchased at a lower price point, raising questions about whether As Ever’s branding is driving the premium.

The discussion intensified after shoppers highlighted a similar Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc sold by British retailer Laithwaites for around $21. The comparison has led critics to question whether Markle ’s name and the As Ever label are enough to justify the difference.

A source familiar with the reaction told RadarOnline.com the comparisons were unavoidable given the type of product Markle has chosen to launch.

“Meghan is positioning As Ever as an aspirational lifestyle label rather than trying to compete with supermarket or high-street pricing, but inevitably people are going to make comparisons,” the source said.

“Sauvignon Blanc from Marlborough is widely available, so shoppers can very quickly see what other bottles cost and some have questioned whether Meghan’s name justifies paying significantly more.”

As Ever selling a lifestyle experience

The wine represents the latest expansion of As Ever, which Markle has built around themes of food, entertaining, and home living.

Rather than marketing the Sauvignon Blanc purely as a drink, the brand has positioned it as part of a wider experience focused on gatherings and special occasions.

“Whether poured alongside a leisurely lunch or raised in a spontaneous toast, each bottle is made for sharing,” Markle says in the product description.

Customers purchasing a case of 12 bottles are also offered three additional bottles as part of a promotional deal.

The launch follows previous As Ever products, including fruit preserves, honey, herbal teas, baking mixes, and flower sprinkles. The company developed from Markle ’s earlier American Riviera Orchard project before being rebranded ahead of its official commercial rollout.

The Duchess of Sussex has used As Ever to build on her long-standing interest in cooking and hosting, an area she previously explored through her lifestyle website The Tig.

The brand has also been closely linked to her Netflix series With Love, Meghan, where she shares recipes, entertaining ideas, and personal touches from her California lifestyle.

Supporters of the company argue that premium celebrity-backed brands often rely on more than the product itself, with packaging, storytelling, and personal connection playing a major role in the buying experience.

Celebrity brands continue facing price comparisons

The reaction to As Ever’s wine highlights a wider challenge faced by celebrity businesses. When products enter crowded markets, consumers often compare them directly with established alternatives that may offer similar features at lower prices.

Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc is produced by numerous wineries across different price ranges, meaning customers have plenty of options when deciding what represents good value.

A marketing source said the response shows the challenge Markle faces as As Ever expands.

“The latest wine release and the reaction to it show Meghan’s pricing strategy will continue facing scrutiny as consumers compare As Ever products with established alternatives,” the source said.

The debate is unlikely to disappear as As Ever continues growing its product range.

While critics question whether the brand premium is justified, the company’s strategy remains focused on selling a curated lifestyle built around Markle ’s personal identity and approach to entertaining.

articles.title: Harry and Meghan land back in the UK with their kids to begin new chapter
articles.standfirst: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's return to Britain marks a major change for their family six years after leaving royal life
articles.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's return to Britain marks a major change for their family six years after leaving royal life
articles.body:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have officially returned to the United Kingdom with their two children, marking a significant new chapter for the family six years after they stepped away from royal duties and established a life in California.

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex arrived in Britain on Wednesday, August 26, with Prince Archie , seven, and Princess Lilibet , five. According to a report from The Telegraph, the family flew privately from California and landed at Birmingham Airport around lunchtime.

Their arrival comes after reports that they planned to spend an “extended” period in Britain.

The move represents a striking reversal from the decision Harry and Meghan made in 2020, when they relinquished their roles as senior working royals and relocated to North America. The episode became widely known as “Megxit,” and the couple subsequently built an independent life in Montecito, California.

This time, however, their return does not mean a return to royal duties. Harry and Meghan are expected to continue their separate commercial and charitable projects rather than resume official responsibilities on behalf of the monarchy.

Reports indicate they will live in a private, non-royal property rather than a royal residence.

The biggest immediate change for the family will be the children's education. Archie and Lilibet have reportedly been enrolled in British schools and are expected to begin classes in September.

It will be a new experience for both children, particularly Lilibet , who was born in California after her parents had already left Britain.

Harry and Meghan's return brings them closer to King Charles

Family appears to be an important factor behind the decision to spend more time in Britain.

Harry's relationship with his father, King Charles III , has shown signs of improvement after years of tension. In July, Harry , Meghan and their children reunited with Charles and Queen Camilla at Highgrove House in Gloucestershire.

The meeting was particularly significant because Charles had not seen Archie and Lilibet in person since 2022.

The Sussexes' latest move could allow the children to spend considerably more time with their grandfather, while also giving Harry an opportunity to strengthen his relationship with the King.

The family is reportedly considering the Cotswolds as a longer-term base. The area would put them relatively close to Highgrove, where Charles and Camilla spend significant time, while still providing considerable distance from the main royal household in Windsor.

Royal commentator Tom Sykes previously highlighted the personal significance of the area for Harry.

“Obviously, that’s where he grew up, living with his father and brother there, and has happy memories,” Sykes said.

The potential choice of the Cotswolds would also underline the distinction between Harry and Meghan's new life in Britain and their former royal existence. They are not returning to official duties or moving back into a palace.

Instead, they appear to be seeking a private family life while rebuilding connections with relatives.

That distinction is particularly important given that their relationship with Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, remains strained.

William and Catherine are based in Windsor, roughly two hours from the Cotswolds, meaning Harry and Meghan could be geographically closer to the Wales family without necessarily resolving the underlying tensions.

The Sussexes are also expected to retain their home and business interests in the United States. Meghan's lifestyle brand and Harry's charitable commitments can continue despite the family's temporary or extended presence in Britain.

For Harry , the move therefore represents neither a complete return to royal life nor a rejection of the California chapter he and Meghan built after 2020.

Instead, it appears to be an attempt to establish a new balance, one that allows their children to experience more of their father's homeland and royal family while preserving the independence the couple fought to establish.

After years defined by separation and public disagreements, the arrival of the Sussex family in Britain could ultimately prove to be one of the most consequential developments in Harry's relationship with the royal family since Megxit.

articles.title: Meghan Markle once again exposed for "extremely rude" behavior in professional setting
articles.standfirst: The Duchess of Sussex is in the spotlight yet again for the wrong reasons.
articles.summary: The Duchess of Sussex is in the spotlight yet again for the wrong reasons.
articles.body:
Practically ever since she met Prince Harry , media tabloids have looked for anything negative to say about Meghan Markle . That eventually caused the married couple to move their family to the West Coast of the United States .

Still, that didn't stop explosive reports about Markle's behavior from surfacing. In particular, accounts from people who have worked close to her during her business ventures haven't exactly had glowing things to say . This week, another report came out that adds more fuel to the fire.

Meghan Markle exhibited odd and rude behavior while interviewing potential household staff in the UK

Page Six dropped an exclusive report with quotes from sources that detailed her "extremely rude" behavior during the interview process for potential employees of hers ; specifically while she was previously in the United Kingdom .

When Meghan was previously living in the UK, the way she interviewed household staff was extremely rude. Applicants would come in to interview for housekeeping or maid positions and were basically forbidden from speaking to her. They would hand over their résumé, then be told to stand off to the side of the room, not speak and not make eye contact while Meghan sat there and reviewed it. She wouldn’t ask them questions or have any kind of actual conversation with them. She would take her time reading through the résumé, look the person up and down and then simply tell them they could leave.

Sarah Jones of Page Six believes this could lead to a lot of household staff members not even interviewing to work for Markle and Harry now that the couple are back in the UK.

At this point, there are too many different accounts of Markle's behavior to disregard them.
